$comment: Upstream-contribution ledger. Every issue/PR Atrium opens against a provider (openclaw/openclaw, NousResearch/hermes-agent) lives here with its state, the protocol frames it is tied to, and the Atrium lots it originated from — so 'which upstream items caused or resulted from our work, and where do they stand' is one read, not an archaeology. Validated by bridge/test/contrib-registry.test.ts; synchronized by bridge/scripts/contrib-sync.mjs (gh, read-only); the process that writes entries is .claude/skills/upstream-contrib/. Rules: public upstream URLs only — never client data, tokens, private paths, or conversational content. States mirror GitHub (open/closed/merged) with `resolution` carrying the human verdict (accepted/rejected/fixed/wontfix/superseded) once known; `origin` says whether the item came from an Atrium finding or from an upstream change Atrium had to adapt to.

entries.title: Plugin context engines cannot increment /status compaction count
entries.why: NOT opened by Atrium — recorded because it falsifies a tempting diagnosis: a chat whose compaction history shows only `manual` checkpoints has NOT necessarily gone unprotected, since a plugin context engine cannot increment that counter at all. Any reasoning built on that history must carry this caveat until the issue closes.

entries.title: Feature request: background-only deferred compaction drain to avoid mid-turn/tool-loop stalls
entries.why: Recorded because it establishes, from production observation, that the host calls the context engine's assemble() PER TOOL-LOOP ITERATION — the fact that decides how a mid-turn overflow under a context engine is triaged (the plugin bundle alone suggests the opposite: it registers no tool_result lifecycle hook). It also names the operative mechanism: under the default deferred threshold mode, crossing the threshold inside a tool loop records debt instead of compacting, so the next model call can still go out oversized.

entries.title: Assembly can target ~100% of tokenBudget and still trigger provider context_length_exceeded
entries.why: The neighbouring failure mode, kept apart on purpose: there the assembly fills the budget to ~99.9% and the provider still rejects it. Not the same as a turn that starts well below the threshold and grows past it — recorded so the two are not conflated the next time a context overflow is triaged.

entries.title: Ignored sessions get no compaction from any layer: global ownsCompaction claim + estimatedTokens: 0 self-report
entries.why: Confirms independently that excluding sessions from the engine leaves them with NO compaction from any layer, because the ownsCompaction claim stays global. Recorded so that ignoreSessionPatterns is never recommended as a way to scope the engine per agent.

entries.title: fix: agent turns fail with reading 'trim' after an attachment enters session history
entries.why: Consumer-side guard in @openclaw/ai transcript-transform: transformAssistant treats every non-thinking/text block as a ToolCall and calls block.id.trim(), while the gateway's own managed-media path persists {type:"attachment"} display blocks into the assistant message it stores — so one delivered file poisons the session and every later turn throws before any model call. Reproduced on v2026.8.2 (0965053) and still unguarded on main and v2026.9.1-beta.1; the same guard existed in src/agents/tool-call-id.ts before the transform moved into @openclaw/ai, which is why 2026.7.1 tolerated the same persisted blocks. Complementary to upstream #135185 (producer side, merged on main, unreleased). Proven red on the pinned file with upstream's own unit config, green with the guard; a build-time distribution patch carries it in the meantime (openclaw-docker/patch-attachment-block.mjs).
